title: Returning Owned Values
story: A factory takes raw materials, builds a product, and hands it to you. In XIOM, functions are factories — they create values and return ownership to the caller.
why: Returning owned values is how data flows through your program — factories create, functions transform, and ownership chains keep everything clean and safe.
analogy: Returning an owned value is like a bakery handing you a fresh loaf of bread — they made it, now it's yours to take home and use.
try_it: Write a function that builds and returns a Vec[Int] with 5 elements. Chain it through another function that doubles each value and returns the modified Vec.
tips: Returning a local variable moves ownership — the compiler handles cleanup automatically
Factory functions (that create and return) are a common and safe pattern
Chaining functions that take and return ownership creates clean data pipelines
Return values don't need clone — returning is always a move, never a copy
common_mistakes: Trying to return a reference (&) to a local variable — the local variable is destroyed
Forgetting that returning consumes the value — you can't use it in the function after return
Cloning a value just to return it — return already moves ownership safely
